hints: Focus on what density tells you about a gas, since mass per volume can be scaled up to mass per mole.
Multiply the given density by the room-condition molar volume of 24000 cm3 mol-1 to find the Mr is about 84.
Think about oxidative cleavage of the C=C bond, and ask which C6 alkene is symmetrical enough to give two identical acid fragments.
walkthrough:
**Find Mr from gas density**

Remember 1 mole of any gas occupies $24000 \text{ cm}^3$ under room conditions. So scale up the density to molar mass.

$$M_r = \text{density} \times \text{molar volume} = (3.50 \times 10^{-3}) \times 24000 = 84$$

**Check which options match Mr 84**

Z is a hydrocarbon alkene with general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$. Test the options.

$$\text{but-2-ene, C}_4\text{H}_8: M_r = (4 \times 12) + 8 = 56$$
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12} \text{ isomers: } M_r = (6 \times 12) + 12 = 84$$

**Use oxidative cleavage to test symmetry**

Hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the C=C bond completely. Each C of the double bond becomes the C of a C=O group in an acid or ketone.

$$\text{RCH=CHR'} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH + R'COOH}$$

**Pick the alkene giving only one acid**

Only a symmetrical alkene gives two identical fragments. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ cleaves to two identical molecules:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Conclude identity of Z**

This matches both clues, Mr of 84 and one single carboxylic acid product, propanoic acid. That is hex-3-ene.

options.A: but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, is symmetrical and would give only ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. However its Mr is 56, not 84, so it does not match the density data.
options.B: 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=C(CH}_3)_2$, has Mr 84 but both C=C carbons have no H. Cleavage gives propanone, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$, a ketone, not a carboxylic acid. So it fails the acid condition.
options.C: hex-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, has Mr 84 but is unsymmetrical. Cleavage gives two different acids, ethanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and butanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.
options.D: hex-3-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, has Mr 84 which matches the density calculation. It is symmetrical about the C=C bond, so oxidative cleavage gives two moles of the same acid, propanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.
